requirements.title: The dashboard lists only notifications the user may see
requirements.statement: The dashboard MUST list only the notifications the signed-in user may see, under the scope ruled for q-notification-list-scope.
requirements.why: An unscoped list leaks another organisation's notifications.

acceptance.text: Given two users in different organisations each with a notification, when either user opens their dashboard, then only notifications within the ruled scope are listed.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A dashboard listing a notification outside the ruled scope.

sources.quote: Should a user see only their own organisation's notifications?

requirements.title: The dashboard lists only the user's own organisation
requirements.statement: The dashboard MUST list only notifications created under the signed-in user's current organisation.

acceptance.text: Given a notification created under another organisation, when the user opens the dashboard, then it is not listed.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A dashboard listing a notification from another organisation.

sources.quote: Should a user see only their own organisation's notifications?

requirements.title: The dashboard lists only notifications the user created
requirements.statement: The dashboard MUST list only notifications the signed-in user created, across organisations.

acceptance.text: Given a notification another colleague created in the same organisation, when the user opens the dashboard, then it is not listed.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A dashboard listing a colleague's notification.

sources.quote: Should a user see only their own organisation's notifications?

requirements.title: The house rules live in a tracked document
requirements.statement: The house rules MUST live in a tracked best-practice document that the code-style bundles include.
requirements.why: Rules in one person's memory never reach other people, CI or another person's build.

acceptance.text: Given the tracked house-rules document, when a style bundle is baked for a Node file, then the bundle includes the house rules.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A baked style bundle without the house rules after they are tracked.

sources.quote: The house-rules asymmetry is the most important thing any candidate found.

requirements.title: The notification view shows only notifications the user may see
requirements.statement: The notification view MUST show only the notification the signed-in user may see, under the scope ruled for q-notification-list-scope.
requirements.why: An unscoped view leaks another organisation's notification.

acceptance.text: Given a notification outside the ruled scope, when the user requests its view directly, then it is refused.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A notification view reachable outside the ruled scope.

requirements.title: The notification view scopes to the user's own organisation
requirements.statement: The notification view MUST show only a notification created under the signed-in user's current organisation.

acceptance.text: Given a notification created under another organisation, when the user requests its view, then it is refused.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A notification view reachable from another organisation.

sources.quote: Should a user see only their own organisation's notifications?

requirements.title: The notification view scopes to notifications the user created
requirements.statement: The notification view MUST show only a notification the signed-in user created, across organisations.

acceptance.text: Given a colleague's notification in the same organisation, when the user requests its view, then it is refused.

requirements.falsifiedBy: A notification view reachable for a colleague's notification.

questions.headline: Should a user see only their own organisation's notifications?
questions.question: The dashboard and notification view list notifications. Which notifications may a signed-in user see?
questions.inPlay: The dashboard list and the notification view, in the plants frontend.

options.text: Only notifications created under the user's current organisation.
options.consequence: Colleagues in one organisation see each other's work; nobody sees another organisation's.

options.text: Only notifications the user personally created, across organisations.
options.consequence: An agent working for two importers sees both; colleagues see nothing of each other's.

ifNobodyAnswers.consequence: Nothing that lists notifications is built. inc-001 stays blocked.

questions.headline: Where should the four house rules live, so Codex and people see them too?
questions.question: Four house rules live in memory and reach only one executor's style reviewers. Where should they live?
questions.inPlay: Every style review task, and the code-style skill's bundles.

options.text: Keep them in memory, and point both executors at the memory files by path.
options.consequence: Both executors see the same rules. The increment that moves them into a tracked document is deferred.

options.text: Move them into a tracked best-practice document that the code-style bundles include.
options.consequence: Everyone and every executor sees the same rules.

ifNobodyAnswers.consequence: Both executors read the rules by path, and inc-002 is deferred until Sam rules.
ifNobodyAnswers.defaultWhy: Moving the rules changes the code-style bundles the whole team uses, a standard only Sam owns.

questions.headline: What may the judges panel decide without you?
questions.question: When sources disagree and the precedence rules cannot settle it, a panel of three judges and a chair rules. Which rulings may it make on its own?
questions.inPlay: The distiller's panel phase and every conflict it settles.

options.text: The panel rules anything the sources, precedence and Sam's standing rulings can settle.
options.consequence: Fewer questions reach Sam, and Sam sees every panel call afterwards.

ifNobodyAnswers.consequence: The panel rules within option A's limits, and each ruling is listed for Sam to reverse.

assumptions.text: Until Sam rules, every task that writes or reviews code reads the four house rules by path from the files they live in today.
